traits.notes: The seedling displays a distinct cluster of lanceolate leaves at the apex of a slender, dark stem. The leaves have a glossy surface and smooth margins. Some leaves exhibit small holes, indicating physical damage. The overall architecture is consistent with a tropical tree seedling in the understory.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached singly at different nodes along the stem, alternating sides, as seen in the side views)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are densely packed towards the distal end of the shoot)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade attached to the stem by a petiole)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (leaf margins are smooth without teeth, though some have physical holes)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are long and narrow, tapering at both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (leaf tips taper to a slender point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaf base tapers to the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with lateral veins branching off it)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, fine, and numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible as fine lines running parallel to the leaf margin)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the leaf surface reflects light, indicating a smooth, glossy texture)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs are visible on the leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (the petioles are very short, appearing almost sessile)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear cylindrical and rounded in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (the stem appears rigid and lignified, typical of a tree seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem appears smooth and hairless)
    19. Stem color: dark brown (the stem is a dark, reddish-brown color)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears smooth without obvious ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling displays a distinct cluster of lanceolate leaves at the apex of a slender, dark stem. The leaves have a glossy surface and smooth margins. Some leaves exhibit small holes, indicating physical damage. The overall architecture is consistent with a tropical tree seedling in the understory.
